record.text: Among ERC Starting Grants working on early handwritten sources, how do projects apply physical-science methods to the surviving objects themselves - imaging or dating the material - to recover evidence that reading their written content cannot supply?

record.reference_answer: Three of the ERC Starting Grants in this group take instruments to the objects rather than only to their contents. HandsandBible applied image processing and pattern recognition to high-resolution multispectral images of the Dead Sea Scrolls in order to identify anonymous scribes, and had radiocarbon testing performed on 30 samples, using the C14 data to train a date-prediction model - an empirical basis for dating scrolls that carry no internal date. ELEPHANTINE combined methods from digital humanities, physics and mathematics to virtually unfold a papyrus package and read its text without physically opening it, and to identify joins between papyrus fragments held in more than 60 institutions. MEDEA-CHART examined medieval and early modern nautical charts under special lighting and with cartometric and numerical modelling, looking for hidden graphic content and for traces of use at sea such as marks left by dry point compasses or pencils.

OUT: 637533 BIFLOW (catalogue and database of bilingual texts; philological, no instrumentation); 677638 ACO (structural/philological analysis of the Acts; its computing is OCR and spellchecking of transcribed texts, i.e. reading content); 716538 MedPub (history of publishing, no material analysis); 758855 TheTocharianTrek (historical linguistics); 802210 PASSIM (digital network of manuscripts built from textual criticism); 802645 KaraimBible (computer-aided digital critical edition, text-level); 803624 SHIVADHARMA (text edition, epigraphy, iconography); 847428 TiNT (analysis of titles as paratexts, text-level); 850604 PeopleAndWriting (graphical/textual/historical analysis, manuscript-studies methods, no instruments); 851393 SYRASP (prison literature plus oral-history interviews); 948150 DYBBUK (AI-powered OCR trained to decipher handwritten Yiddish - computing applied to read the written content, which the question explicitly excludes); 948152 NOTA (codicology and palaeography, no instrumentation); 948497 BOMPAC (statistical and palaeographical study of digitized fragments; quantitative but no physical measurement of the objects); 949710 ACADEMIA (codicology, palaeography, Digital Humanities on the corpus). record.reference_answer: Three of the ERC Starting Grants in this group take instruments to the objects rather than only to their contents. MEDEA-CHART examined medieval and early modern nautical charts under special lighting and with cartometric and numerical modelling, looking for hidden graphic content and for traces of use at sea such as marks left by dry point compasses or pencils.

record.reference_answer: Three of the ERC Starting Grants in this group take instruments to the objects rather than only to their contents. HandsandBible applied image processing and pattern recognition to high-resolution multispectral images of the Dead Sea Scrolls in order to identify anonymous scribes, and had radiocarbon testing performed on 30 samples, using the C14 data to train a date-prediction model - an empirical basis for dating scrolls that carry no internal date. ELEPHANTINE combined methods from digital humanities, physics and mathematics to virtually unfold a papyrus package and read its text without physically opening it, and to identify joins between papyrus fragments held in more than 60 institutions. MEDEA-CHART examined medieval and early modern nautical charts under special lighting and with cartometric and numerical modelling, looking for hidden graphic content and for traces of use at sea such as marks left by dry point compasses or pencils.

record.text: Among ERC Starting Grant projects whose abstract mentions autism, which ones carry out their experiments in a non-human species, and which species do they use?

record.reference_answer: Nine of the 29 ERC Starting Grants whose abstract mentions autism run their experiments in a non-human species; the other 20 work with human participants, human cohorts or human data. Rodents dominate: THERAUTISM screens molecular targets and a gene-therapy vector in preclinical mouse models of ASD, REVERSEAUTISM pairs Slc7a5 and BCKDK mutant mice with human cerebral organoids, DisConn images the awake mouse and maps the mouse axonal connectome, SafeFate characterises Myt1l knockout mice alongside human induced neurons, and NEUROGOAL and MotivatedBehaviors both record from circuits in behaving mice. Three step outside rodents - HomeoBalanceExcInh dissects excitation/inhibition balance in Drosophila Kenyon cells, MultiSense records whole-brain activity in larval zebrafish, and Brain2Bee tests its dopamine model in the honey bee.

The adjudication test is whether the project's own text shows it carrying out experiments in a named non-human species. IN (9): 639489 HomeoBalanceExcInh - Drosophila Kenyon-cell circuit, 'allowing flies to learn to discriminate between different odours'; 677878 NEUROGOAL - two-photon imaging in 'foraging mice' and a mouse model of autism; 715508 REVERSEAUTISM - 'Employing a series of mouse models', plus human cerebral organoids; 715980 MultiSense - 'brain-wide response of larval zebrafish'; 757583 Brain2Bee - 'an animal model, the honey bee'; 802371 DisConn - 'recordings in the awake mouse', 'mouse axonal connectome'; 804710 SafeFate - 'new Myt1l knockout mouse models'; 851231 THERAUTISM - 'the most suitable and robust preclinical mouse models of ASD'; 949652 MotivatedBehaviors - 'I characterized in mice a novel circuit', mouse models of psychiatric disease. record.text: Among ERC Starting Grant projects whose abstract mentions autism, which ones carry out their experiments in a non-human species, and which species do they use?

filter_evidence.filter_sql: SELECT p.id FROM project p WHERE (p.objective ILIKE '%autis%' OR p.title ILIKE '%autis%') AND p.fundingScheme = 'ERC-STG' ORDER BY p.id

record.reference_answer: Nine of the 29 ERC Starting Grants whose abstract mentions autism run their experiments in a non-human species; the other 20 work with human participants, human cohorts or human data. Rodents dominate: THERAUTISM screens molecular targets and a gene-therapy vector in preclinical mouse models of ASD, REVERSEAUTISM pairs Slc7a5 and BCKDK mutant mice with human cerebral organoids, DisConn images the awake mouse and maps the mouse axonal connectome, SafeFate characterises Myt1l knockout mice alongside human induced neurons, and NEUROGOAL and MotivatedBehaviors both record from circuits in behaving mice. Three step outside rodents - HomeoBalanceExcInh dissects excitation/inhibition balance in Drosophila Kenyon cells, MultiSense records whole-brain activity in larval zebrafish, and Brain2Bee tests its dopamine model in the honey bee.
record.notes: Filter: fundingScheme = 'ERC-STG' plus the '%autis%' text condition over objective and title, which is what makes the survivor set enumerable (29 survivors). The question's anchor is worded to describe exactly what the filter reads - the project's own abstract - so a project whose only autism tie is in its published report (e.g. 637591 NEURAL AS, whose report mentions 'autistic spectrum disorders' while its abstract does not) is outside the question as well as outside the survivor set. At the runtime the structured half carries only fundingScheme; the topical half falls to retrieval (scoped.py whitelists no subject-matter column). Adjudication was exhaustive: all 29 survivor objectives read, plus workPerformed/finalResults for every IN and borderline case, plus a survivor-scoped SQL species sweep (mouse/mice, rat/rodent, zebrafish, Drosophila/flies, honey bee, monkey/macaque/primate/ferret/C. elegans over objective + report text). The adjudication test is whether the project's own text shows it carrying out experiments in a named non-human species. IN (9): 639489 HomeoBalanceExcInh - Drosophila Kenyon-cell circuit, 'allowing flies to learn to discriminate between different odours'; 677878 NEUROGOAL - two-photon imaging in 'foraging mice' and a mouse model of autism; 715508 REVERSEAUTISM - 'Employing a series of mouse models', plus human cerebral organoids; 715980 MultiSense - 'brain-wide response of larval zebrafish'; 757583 Brain2Bee - 'an animal model, the honey bee'; 802371 DisConn - 'recordings in the awake mouse', 'mouse axonal connectome'; 804710 SafeFate - 'new Myt1l knockout mouse models'; 851231 THERAUTISM - 'the most suitable and robust preclinical mouse models of ASD'; 949652 MotivatedBehaviors - 'I characterized in mice a novel circuit', mouse models of psychiatric disease. OUT (20): 636458 CogSoCoAGE, 676943 SLAB, 678286 CONTEXTVISION, 678733 CAASD, 679927 SYNAPLAST MR, 715824 POINTS, 716974 Becoming Social, 755816 AUTISMS, 801708 ANTICIPATE, 801715 PUPILTRAITS, 804881 NEUROEPIGENETHICS, 852570 CoCoFlex, 852885 INDIVISUAL, 853211 DEVCOM, 946228 DEFEND, 948545 TrackingMinds, 950010 FamilySleeps - human participants, human cohorts, human imaging/gaze/pupillometry data, algorithms or ethics work, with no species keyword anywhere in objective or report text; plus three that do experimental biology without ever showing an experiment in a named species - 716011 NANOGLU ('synaptic proteins endogenously expressed in neurons'), 950013 CERCODE ('models of early cerebellar disruptions'), and 803984 GIDE, whose only species word in the whole record is the abstract's closing CV clause 'my extensive training in viral and mouse genetic techniques' while all four report sections (lineage barcoding, single-cell transcriptomics, membrane-potential perturbation) name no organism. - 757583 Brain2Bee - objective: "Brain2Bee will investigate whether DAMS generalises to an animal model, the honey bee".
- 802371 DisConn - objective: "a novel combination of rsfMRI and advanced neural manipulations and recordings in the awake mouse"; report: "an unprecedented high-resolution analysis of the mouse axonal connectome".
- 804710 SafeFate - report: "we have generated and studied new Myt1l knockout mouse models and CRISPR-engineered human induced neurons. MYT1L-deficient mice displayed striking neurological and behavioural phenotypes".
- 851231 THERAUTISM - report: "we have successfully identified the most suitable and robust preclinical mouse models of ASD, implemented all required techniques, and set up the experimental conditions in the laboratory."

- 803984 GIDE (dropped from gold in the fix round) - the only species word in its entire record is the objective's CV clause "This proposal takes full advantage of my extensive training in viral and mouse genetic techniques, single-cell transcriptomic data processing, and in vivo manipulation of neuronal activity." - 950013 CERCODE - "we successfully developed models of early cerebellar disruptions"; no species named.

It fills the scheme axis (ERC-STG) and the social-sciences/psychology bucket for the hybrid route, and it is the first hybrid entry whose textual ask is a methodological property rather than a topical one. The L3 filter-survey label is computed: 9 gold out of 29 enumerated survivors, above the subtype's floor of 5 and inside its 5-60 survivor window, with the group pattern - rodents dominate, three exceptions - being what the answer has to state.

- SCOPED-RETRIEVABLE - PASS. The drafter's own single k=20 run reached 6 of the accepted members; the independent reviewer's re-measurements reached 9 of 10, 10 of 10, and (at the new 29-project scope) 8 of 9 inside some condition's top-20. All figures are recorded in notes so the difference is visible rather than hidden.
- TERM-STYLE-HONEST - PASS. No gold text contains "non-human", "species" or "carry out their experiments"; inside the scope the lexical channel ranks human-participant non-gold projects first (CAASD 1, DEVCOM 2).
- ONE-QUESTION - PASS. One ask - which survivors work in a non-human species - with the species as the detail of that same answer.
- REFERENCE-FIDELITY - PASS as rewritten: GIDE removed, counts restated as "Nine of the 29" and "the other 20", the mouse sentence naming only projects that state mouse work outright. findings.claim: The whole gold boundary now turns on one project. 803984 GIDE is the only project in the 29 whose abstract names a non-human species while its report names none, and a solver reading its abstract can defensibly answer 'GIDE - mouse' and be scored wrong.
findings.evidence: A channel-split sweep over all 29 survivors (a 50-term species list run separately over objective and over teaser||summary||workPerformed||finalResults) returned, for GIDE, in_abstract ['mouse'], in_report [] - unique in the set. Every other gold is species-positive in the report (REVERSEAUTISM and THERAUTISM are the mirror case, report-only), and all 19 OUTs are empty in both channels. The GIDE clause reads as a training credential or as a statement of what the proposal will use, and neither read is strained. GIDE is retrievable inside the scope: on the reviewer's round-1 scoped query it ranked dense 5, hybrid 9, hybrid_rerank 10.
findings.fix_direction: Make the discriminator explicit in the question rather than only in notes - e.g. 'which ones describe carrying out experiments in a non-human species'. Alternatively leave as recorded and accept a one-project scoring wobble; the reviewer sees no edit that removes the ambiguity from GIDE's own sentence.
findings.ruling_why: Real and correctly severity-tagged: GIDE is the one project whose species word sits in the abstract and nowhere in the report, so a solver can defensibly return it - but the question's own test ('carry out their experiments in') already leans against a training-credential clause, the report names no organism, and 8 of 9 gold plus all 19 OUTs are unambiguous under either read. One item of a nine-item answer is a scoring wobble, not a change in what the cell measures, and the critic itself states no edit removes the ambiguity from GIDE's sentence.

findings.claim: The reference's first sentence characterises the entire 20-project complement as human work, but three of those twenty are bench biology with no human participants and no named species - a distinction the entry's own notes draws correctly.
findings.evidence: reference_answer: 'Nine of the 29 ... run their experiments in a non-human species; the other 20 work with human participants, human cohorts or human data.' Against the text: GIDE's four report sections describe genetic barcodes, single-cell transcriptomic and functional perturbation approaches, and selectively altering membrane potential - no human participants, no cohort, no human dataset. NANOGLU: 'we have developed genome editing technologies to precisely tag synaptic proteins endogenously expressed in neurons'. CERCODE: 'we successfully developed models of early cerebellar disruptions'. notes states this accurately, so the defect is confined to the reference text - the artifact answers are scored against.
findings.fix_direction: A one-clause reference edit, no re-measurement needed: '...the other 20 work with human participants, human cohorts or human data, or - in three cases (GIDE, NANOGLU, CERCODE) - do experimental biology whose text never names the organism.'
findings.ruling_why: Upheld in substance - GIDE, NANOGLU and CERCODE are bench biology with no human participants and the reference's complement clause calls all 20 human work - but the defect is confined to one clause of prose about the projects that are not the answer, the entry's own notes state the distinction correctly, and the scored content (which nine projects, which species) is untouched.

judge_decisions.rationale: The round-1 HIGH is gone on executed evidence, not on assertion: the fresh derivation at the new boundary returns 0 rows outside the filter and 29 of 29 survivors carrying the term in the abstract, so the question's words and the recorded scope now denote the same set and NEURAL AS is out by wording rather than by oversight. What remains is a nine-project filter-survey with a clean species discriminator, 8 of 9 gold retrievable in some condition's top-20 at the new scope, and two MIDs that cost at most one item and one clause of complement prose - neither moves the level, the route, the subtype or the term_style. The within-candidate stop rule does not fire: the class the fix round targeted was cleared, and what the critic found this round is residual ambiguity in one project's own text rather than the same defect surviving. Both MIDs ride into the report as notes for the promote-time veto, together with the LOW about 'record from circuits'.

record.text: Among ERC Starting Grants working on early handwritten sources, how do projects apply physical-science methods to the surviving objects themselves - imaging or dating the material - to recover evidence that reading their written content cannot supply?

filter_evidence.filter_sql: SELECT p.id FROM project p WHERE (p.objective ILIKE '%manuscript%' OR p.title ILIKE '%manuscript%') AND p.fundingScheme = 'ERC-STG' ORDER BY p.id

record.reference_answer: Three of the ERC Starting Grants in this group take instruments to the objects rather than only to their contents. HandsandBible applied image processing and pattern recognition to high-resolution multispectral images of the Dead Sea Scrolls in order to identify anonymous scribes, and had radiocarbon testing performed on 30 samples, using the C14 data to train a date-prediction model - an empirical basis for dating scrolls that carry no internal date. ELEPHANTINE combined methods from digital humanities, physics and mathematics to virtually unfold a papyrus package and read its text without physically opening it, and to identify joins between papyrus fragments held in more than 60 institutions. MEDEA-CHART examined medieval and early modern nautical charts under special lighting and with cartometric and numerical modelling, looking for hidden graphic content and for traces of use at sea such as marks left by dry point compasses or pencils.
record.notes: Filter: fundingScheme='ERC-STG' (structural, the part the runtime scoped path can express) combined with a manuscript text condition over title/objective; 17 survivors, inside the filter-synthesize window of 5-20. Corpus-wide the manuscript text condition alone matches 131 projects, so the scheme constraint does the narrowing. record.text: Among ERC Starting Grants working on early handwritten sources, how do projects apply physical-science methods to the surviving objects themselves - imaging or dating the material - to recover evidence that reading their written content cannot supply?

record.reference_answer: Three of the ERC Starting Grants in this group take instruments to the objects rather than only to their contents. HandsandBible applied image processing and pattern recognition to high-resolution multispectral images of the Dead Sea Scrolls in order to identify anonymous scribes, and had radiocarbon testing performed on 30 samples, using the C14 data to train a date-prediction model - an empirical basis for dating scrolls that carry no internal date. ELEPHANTINE combined methods from digital humanities, physics and mathematics to virtually unfold a papyrus package and read its text without physically opening it, and to identify joins between papyrus fragments held in more than 60 institutions. MEDEA-CHART examined medieval and early modern nautical charts under special lighting and with cartometric and numerical modelling, looking for hidden graphic content and for traces of use at sea such as marks left by dry point compasses or pencils.
